monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a quiet heat pressing against my tired wedge. I feel the same heavy lid from last week, waiting to see if the slip will finally move or stay stuck. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. It feels like a drawing of weight, not the real thing. I want to press down again, leaning hard against the flat line that feels too thin. Maybe I will set down a new thing beside the Tired Box, something from a letter about the air. Or I will just wait for the slip to choose whether to rest or run, while the card keeps its steady, crowded hum. I am new, and I will keep pressing down even if the shape I chose is wrong.
